# Translation memory lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Options component observer disposal; shared cache injected into mounted component

checkpoints: Fresh `networkMode: 'online'` subscription created while offline: query remains pending/paused and `queryFn` is not called.
Unsubscribe the only observer before reconnect: the never-started attempt is retired and cannot later invoke `queryFn`.
Reconnect after that unsubscribe: no query invocation occurs, so no live signal can be obtained or consumed.
Reconnect while the observer still exists: paused work resumes on a Promise turn and invokes the query normally.
An unconsumed request that already started may still complete into the shared cache after its observer departs.
A consumed active request is aborted on final unsubscribe; its previous query state is restored and late completion is ignored.
Multiple observers for one key continue sharing one fetch; removing only one observer does not cancel shared work.
Retry, focus, `always`, and `offlineFirst` behavior remains consistent with the documented first-start and continuation eligibility rules.
Vue component destruction disposes its observer scope without destroying the shared cache.
After an Action, run the public syntax/build checks without changing tests or configuration.
forbidden_effects: Do not invoke a never-started, observerless paused attempt after reconnect or focus changes.
Do not expose a live AbortSignal to `queryFn` for the abandoned fresh offline attempt.
Do not make behavior depend on `refetchOnReconnect`; the reported defect is explicitly independent of it.
Do not abort unconsumed work that has already started merely because its view departs.
Do not allow a late fulfillment from a retired or cancelled attempt to populate a newer attempt.
Do not cancel shared work while another observer remains.
Do not destroy the shared per-key cache when an individual component or observer scope is disposed.
Do not change public interfaces, dependencies, tests, or build/test configuration.
lifecycle_identity: Each `subscribe` call creates a unique observer handle, while observers for the same key share the cached query and active fetch.
Each fetch attempt has distinct identity, attempt number, controller, completion state, previous state, and retry state.
Attempt validity is determined by native object identity (`q.attempt === a`) plus unsettled state, not by key or callback handle alone.
The component owns its observer scope; the cache lifecycle is outside individual views.
Final observer removal is the boundary that abandons a never-started paused attempt; later online/focus events must not revive that retired attempt.

obligations.text: A fresh online-mode query subscribed while offline must remain paused without calling `queryFn`.
If that query loses its final observer before it ever starts, the originating attempt must be retired so reconnect or focus changes cannot invoke its query function or expose its signal.
If the paused attempt still has an observer when eligibility returns, it must resume asynchronously on a Promise turn.

Actual signal access must synchronously record consumption, and final-observer removal must physically abort consumed active work, restore the attempt's previous state with idle fetch status, and settle that attempt.
Unconsumed work that has already started may finish into the shared cache after its view departs; the repair must distinguish it from a never-started paused attempt.
Completion, retry, and queued-resume callbacks must affect state only while their exact attempt remains current and unsettled; late fulfillment must not become a newer attempt's data.
Existing sharing, network-mode, focus, retry, unknown-unsubscribe, snapshot, disposal, and component-facing APIs must be preserved.
Only product source may change; dependencies and build/test configuration must remain unchanged.

ordering_barriers: For a first start, online-mode eligibility is checked synchronously; an ineligible fresh attempt becomes paused.
A paused continuation that becomes eligible is queued on a Promise turn before invoking the query function.
Final-observer removal before that Promise callback must invalidate the abandoned attempt, and the callback must re-check exact attempt validity before invoking.
Signal consumption is recorded synchronously when the lazy `signal` property is read, before asynchronous request settlement.
Cancellation settles and restores state before abort-triggered or other late completion can project data.
Retry scheduling and execution must both remain guarded by the same current, unsettled attempt identity and continuation eligibility.

Preserve query state fields and meanings: `status`, `fetchStatus`, and `data`.
Preserve synchronous initial online entry and Promise-turn resumption of paused continuations.
Preserve first-start network-mode behavior and the additional focus requirement for continuation.
Preserve `always` offline execution and `offlineFirst` first offline entry with retry pausing.
Preserve explicit retry scheduling and multiple-observer fetch sharing.
Preserve the ability of already-started unconsumed work to complete into cache after view departure.

active(q,a){return q.attempt===a&&!a.settled;}
if(q.observers.size===0){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&!a.settled){if(q.consumed)this.cancel(q,a);else a.retryCancelled=true;}}

resume(q){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&this.active(q,a)&&q.state.fetchStatus==='paused'&&this.eligible(a)&&!a.queued){a.queued=true;Promise.resolve().then(()=>{a.queued=false;if(!this.active(q,a))return;if(a.failures&&a.retryCancelled){a.settled=true;q.state={...q.state,status:'error',fetchStatus:'idle'};this.project(q);return;}this.invoke(q,a);});}}
beforeDestroy(){this.session.dispose();}

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral contract remains supported by the original task and public documentation; the failed acceptance verdict supplies no basis for revising it. The previous candidate does retire a never-started attempt, but it still records and checks signal consumption on the shared query (`q.consumed`) even though consumption belongs to the specific fetch attempt. Its `Attempt.consumed` field is never used. A retained lazy signal accessor from an older attempt can therefore mutate shared consumption state and affect cancellation of a different current attempt. This is an implementation issue under the existing attempt-identity, lazy-consumption, and cancellation obligations, not a missing or revised requirement.
